title: Noun and particle foundations: existence, space and movement

relationships.label: Existence: いる or ある, including negation
Spatial noun phrases: location of existence or activity
Movement を: route or point of departure

exercises.translation: There is a cat in the garden. Fill the affirmative nonpast existence verb in the ます-series.
exercises.evidence: Choose the ordinary existence predicate for the referent, and preserve the requested polarity and style.
exercises.explanation: Use いる／います for this ordinary animal-existence statement.

options.label: います
options.rationale: Use いる／います for this ordinary animal-existence statement.

options.label: あります
options.rationale: This is the ordinary existence predicate for the other referent class, not this scene.

exercises.translation: The teacher is not in the classroom. Fill the negative nonpast existence verb in the ます-series.
exercises.evidence: Choose the ordinary existence predicate for the referent, and preserve the requested polarity and style.
exercises.explanation: The negative of います is いません; the teacher is absent, not an inanimate object.

options.label: いません
options.rationale: The negative of います is いません; the teacher is absent, not an inanimate object.

options.label: ありません
options.rationale: This is the ordinary existence predicate for the other referent class, not this scene.

exercises.translation: There are flowers in the garden. Fill the affirmative nonpast existence verb in the ます-series.
exercises.evidence: Choose the ordinary existence predicate for the referent, and preserve the requested polarity and style.
exercises.explanation: Plants ordinarily take ある here even though they are biologically alive.

options.label: あります
options.rationale: Plants ordinarily take ある here even though they are biologically alive.

options.label: います
options.rationale: This is the ordinary existence predicate for the other referent class, not this scene.

exercises.translation: There is no desk in the room. Fill the negative nonpast existence verb in the ます-series.
exercises.evidence: Choose the ordinary existence predicate for the referent, and preserve the requested polarity and style.
exercises.explanation: Use ありません for the absence of this inanimate thing; plain ない is a different requested style.

options.label: ありません
options.rationale: Use ありません for the absence of this inanimate thing; plain ない is a different requested style.

options.label: いません
options.rationale: This is the ordinary existence predicate for the other referent class, not this scene.

exercises.translation: There is a book on the desk. Assemble 机 (つくえ, desk) + 上 (うえ, top) with the linking and location particles; fill the whole location phrase.
exercises.evidence: Build the reference-noun + の + spatial-noun phrase, then match the location particle to the supplied predicate.
exercises.explanation: の links the reference object to 上; に marks where the book exists.

options.label: 机の上に
options.rationale: の links the reference object to 上; に marks where the book exists.

options.label: 机の上で
options.rationale: This supplies the other location-predicate frame.

exercises.translation: There is a dog behind the bank. Assemble 銀行 (ぎんこう) + 後ろ (うしろ, behind) with the linking and location particles.
exercises.evidence: Build the reference-noun + の + spatial-noun phrase, then match the location particle to the supplied predicate.
exercises.explanation: 銀行の後ろ is the spatial noun phrase; に locates the dog there.

options.label: 銀行の後ろに
options.rationale: 銀行の後ろ is the spatial noun phrase; に locates the dog there.

options.label: 銀行の後ろで
options.rationale: This supplies the other location-predicate frame.

exercises.translation: I study to the right of the window. Assemble 窓 (まど) + 右 (みぎ, right side) with the linking and location particles.
exercises.evidence: Build the reference-noun + の + spatial-noun phrase, then match the location particle to the supplied predicate.
exercises.explanation: の builds 窓の右 and で marks the place of the studying activity.

options.label: 窓の右で
options.rationale: の builds 窓の右 and で marks the place of the studying activity.

options.label: 窓の右に
options.rationale: This supplies the other location-predicate frame.

exercises.translation: I wait outside the school. Assemble 学校 (がっこう) + 外 (そと, outside) with the linking and activity-location particles.
exercises.evidence: Build the reference-noun + の + spatial-noun phrase, then match the location particle to the supplied predicate.
exercises.explanation: The requested activity-location phrase uses で after 学校の外; に would need a different predicate frame such as いる.

options.label: 学校の外で
options.rationale: The requested activity-location phrase uses で after 学校の外; に would need a different predicate frame such as いる.

options.label: 学校の外に
options.rationale: This supplies the other location-predicate frame.

exercises.translation: I crossed the bridge. 渡る is わたる. Interpret the を phrase: 通り道 (とおりみち, route traversed) or 出発点 (しゅっぱつてん, place/vehicle left behind).
exercises.evidence: The movement verb identifies the relation; を is not always an ordinary object marker.
exercises.explanation: A route is traversed; a departure phrase identifies what is left. Neither requires that place to be physically affected.

options.label: 通り道
options.rationale: This matches the verb's movement relation.

options.label: 出発点
options.rationale: This does not match the verb's movement relation.
